title: MADR export is a disposable owned-directory projection with a round-trip contract
context: Export half of the MADR bridge (import half: dec_8b0f588b93 / commit aa06ecc). Shipped in commit 253fa5f, released v1.16.0.
decision: `hunch export-adr` renders the PUBLIC store's decisions as a regenerated MADR 3.x corpus. The projection OWNS its directory: any hand-written ADR-shaped file (no hunch:generated marker) refuses the whole export — mixing generated files into a real corpus would duplicate NNNN numbering and corrupt every MADR reader of that dir. Numbering is date-ordered per export with two honesty rules: a missing valid_from falls back to the window's valid_to, and on a shared boundary instant the CLOSED window numbers first — a decision can never number after its own successor. Rendering uses canonical MADR phrasing (Chosen option: line + plain Considered Options) so the projection round-trips through import-adr losslessly for status, chosen option, alternatives, and supersede links. Stale generated files from earlier runs (marker-verified as ours) are removed on regeneration. Overlay records never reach the projection — the caller reads store.json.loadAll only. Prints the backstage.io/adr-location annotation.
consequences: Numbers are assigned per export and may shift between runs — the corpus is a disposable build artifact per the compiler thesis, internally consistent but not a stable citation target; the graph ids in each file's source comment are the stable handles.
The whole-dir refusal means a repo that imported its corpus from docs/adr must export to a different directory (the error message says so and suggests one).
Both bridge halves shipped closes the private MADR-bridge roadmap decision.
alternatives_rejected: Per-file clobber checks instead of whole-dir refusal: live-tested first — differently-slugged generated files interleave with hand-written ones and duplicate NNNN numbers without ever colliding on a filename, silently corrupting the corpus for adr-log/Backstage readers.

Stable export numbering (persisting a number allocation): turns the projection into a second source of truth that must be merged and migrated; the compiler thesis says regenerate, and stable citation belongs to decision ids.
Exporting the overlay union behind a flag: a committable artifact must never be one flag away from leaking private records; the one-way privacy boundary stays unconditional.
